rows.title: Goldbach's conjecture for prime-like distributions
rows.statement:
Let $Q$ be a subset of the natural numbers, and let $\pi_Q(n)$ denote the number of elements of $Q$ less than or equal to $n$. Let $\pi(n)$ denote the number of primes less than or equal to $n$. The distribution of $Q$ is **similar to the distribution of primes** if there exists $c\ta\in\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
|\pi_Q(n)-\pi(n)|<c
$$

for every integer $n$.

**Generalization of Goldbach's conjecture.** Let $Q$ be a subset of natural numbers whose distribution is similar to primes. There exists $N_Q\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for any even integer $2n>N_Q$, there exist $q_1,q_2\in Q$ satisfying

$$
q_1+q_2=2n.
$$

This proposes that the Goldbach representation property depends on having a prime-like counting distribution rather than on primality itself. The source gives computational evidence for particular shifted-prime constructions, but does not establish the assertion for every subset with the stated distribution property.
rows.source_name: Ameneh Farhadian, “Goldbach Conjecture: Violation Probability and Generalization to Prime-like Distributions”, arXiv:2504.14353 (2025).
rows.references:
**17 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2004–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2502.03513](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.03513), [arXiv:2301.02770](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.02770), [arXiv:2210.02722](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.02722), [arXiv:2207.09452](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.09452), [arXiv:1912.08043](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.08043), [arXiv:1904.09835](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.09835), [arXiv:1806.00946](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.00946), [arXiv:1804.05561](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.05561), [arXiv:1711.06961](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.06961), [arXiv:1706.00317](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.00317), [arXiv:1611.07251](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.07251), [arXiv:1512.05024](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.05024), and 4 more.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14353

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

purpose: Independent full arbitrary-prime-counting-distribution Goldbach negation, literal/actual-source and substantive/prior qualification; no formal tools
